items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: At the time, I was rehearsing with a group of musicians of whom I can only remember one musician who was Austin "Slim" Moore... I had known "Slim" a long time.

ctx.x: One letter I received from Charles that had no date, mentioned that he almost had a contract for me to play with Charlie "Dizzy" Lewis and "Big Boy" Goudie but he didn't mention where. The next one was dated the 7th of October and mentioned that he was on the verge of getting me a contract in a new club that was going to open and asked me if I was still interested. I wrote immediately and told him, I was and also would agree to the conditions which were not bad.

At the time, I was rehearsing with a group of musicians of whom I can only remember one musician who was Austin "Slim" Moore, a trombonist. I had known "Slim" a long time. He was about 6 feet 4 and weighed 190 or perhaps 200 pounds, and was a long way from actually being slim. The pianist-and leader was a pianist who lived on 135th street between a couple of times a week and we had done a couple of gigs together. Most of the cats were beginning to dig the modern jive and I remember the first one of those numbers…

I had mentioned to some musicians that I may have a chance to go to Europe and when this pianist got the news through the grape wine, I was excluded from the rehearsals. In November, I had some luck and hit the numbers twice for 5 cents and again for 25 cents the first of December.
